And a little later, 'Ala al-Din also died in it. [He was succeeded by] Tegüder his brother, he who was called Ahmad.
When Abaqa, the King of Kings, departed from this world,
all the royal princes assembled with the nobles,
and agreed that Ahmad, the son of Hulagu,
whom Qutui Khatun, the great queen, had borne him,
should stand at the head of the Mongols, those who were in the West,
because the way belonged to him,
and he was the oldest of his brothers.
And when he sat upon the throne of the kingdom on Sunday, the twenty-first of June,
in the year
one thousand five hundred and ninety-three
1593 of the Greeks,
he showed great mercy and open-handed generosity.
And he opened the treasury of his father and of his brother,
and brought out great treasures of gold and silver, and distributed them to his brothers, the emirs, and the Mongol armies.
And he looked upon all nations with an eye of compassion,
especially upon the heads of the Christian confessions.
And he wrote for them patents of exemption from tributes and taxes for all the churches and monasteries, and for the priests and monks in every place and quarter.
And he sent envoys to the ruler of Egypt:
Saba, the atabeg of the ruler of the land of the Romans,
and Qutb al-Din al-Shirazi, the judge of the city of Sebastia,
and Shams al-Din ibn Titi, the vizier of the ruler of Mardin.
And he said to the Egyptians:
"According to the command of God and the law which our father Genghis Khan established for us,
the lot of the kingdom of the Mongols has fallen to me.
And because God has called me to peace,
I desire that everyone in his own region may possess a peaceful and tranquil life,
and that wars, slaughters, and captivities may cease from the face of the earth.
Therefore, if you agree to this,
give your hand to peace and submission.
But if you persist in your rebellion {OCR?},
God will require from you the blood of the oppressed which is shed."
And the ruler of Egypt agreed that there should be peace,
and that the sword should be removed from between them,
yet upon the condition
that the city of Mosul should belong to the son of Badr al-Din,
and that he should give to the Mongols whatever these others were giving,
and likewise also Baghdad and Sinjar.
